About Anthropic

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About Beneficial Deployments 

Beneficial Deployments ensures AI reaches and benefits the communities that need it most. We partner with nonprofits, foundations, and mission-driven organizations to deploy Claude in education, global health, economic mobility, and life sciences — focusing on raising the floor for those who need it most.

About the Role

We're looking for an Applied AI Engineer to join our Beneficial Deployments, Life Sciences team. This is a partner-facing role: you'll support nonprofits, research institutes, academic medical centres and public-sector funders as they use Claude to get treatments to patients with rare and neglected diseases, where there is little or no commercial incentive to fund development.

The role focuses on clinical development, where we think Claude can help these partners today. Trials in these diseases have small patient populations, investigator-led or nonprofit funding and little operational support, and they often stall on protocol quality, operational risk and site start-up. Claude can help teams design better trials and start them sooner. Much of this work is drug repurposing: testing new uses for approved, usually off-patent or generic medicines, whose known safety profiles can let a good hypothesis reach patients years sooner than a new molecule.

You'll advise and embed in partners' teams, building alongside their engineers, scientists and clinicians.

Responsibilities

  • Work with partners' trial teams to design, review and prioritise clinical trials with Claude: drafting and reviewing protocols and statistical analysis plans, and flagging enrolment and operational risks.
  • Build and validate tools that help partners find new uses for approved, mostly off-patent medicines in rare and neglected diseases, from literature, omics and patient data, and assemble the evidence so the partner can decide the next step.
  • Build reusable infrastructure other institutions can adopt (MCP servers for biomedical data sources, agent skills, benchmarks grounded in real clinical questions), and feed what you learn in the field back to product, engineering and research.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You Have

  • Hands-on clinical development experience: designing, running or analysing clinical trials, or assessing clinical evidence to decide which programmes go forward (for example due diligence or asset evaluation). Drug repurposing work as part of that is a strong plus, as is having contributed to a regulatory submission for a trial.
  • Comfort with biomedical data: literature, omics, and real-world patient data (health records, registries, claims), ideally inside secure or trusted research environments.
  • Strong engineering skills: you can take an LLM-powered tool from prototype to production code, and write evals to measure it.
  • Experience working directly with external partners or customers in a technical role.
  • Clear written and verbal communication: docs other institutes can use without you, and results clinicians trust.
  • A scrappy mentality:

About the Role

Together AI is building the AI Native Cloud, an end-to-end platform for the full generative AI lifecycle, combining the fastest LLM inference engine with state-of-the-art GPU cloud infrastructure. The Together Cloud team builds the [Together GPU Clusters](https://www.together.ai/gpu-clusters) flagship IaaS product that provides high-performance, AI-ready GPU clusters through a self-serve cloud console, along with the virtualized infrastructure layer powering Together's inference, RL, and fine-tuning products.

As a Staff Software Engineer focusing on AI Compute in the Together Cloud org, you will set technical direction for and build major components of the next generation AI cloud platform – a highly available, global cloud infrastructure with cutting-edge virtualization of the latest ML hardware: GB300s/VRs, BlueField DPUs, InfiniBand and dual/quad-plane RoCEv2 fabrics. That virtualized computing platform powers our own SaaS products – inference, RL, and fine-tuning – and serves external cloud customers through self-serve offerings such as on-demand/reserved Kubernetes/Slurm clusters, across dozens of data centers and hundreds of thousands of GPUs.

This is an architect-and-build role. Fully automated bootstrapping of GPU data centers, high-performance virtualization of GPU compute and DC networking without compromising isolation or portability, and fault-tolerant decentralized control planes — you'll set the architecture for these across our global and in-DC services, and be a key owner of the hardest parts, in the code as well as the design. Your designs will span the IaaS layer of a greenfield Vera Rubin data center up to the global management plane that schedules capacity across all of them. At this level the job is as much leverage as code: the standards you set and the engineers you grow decide how fast the rest of Together Cloud ships.

  • Own the GPU and network virtualization stack: the hypervisor, kernel, and SDN work that keeps GPU compute and DC networking high-performance, portable, and strongly isolated across heterogeneous hardware.

  • Design the GPU scheduling and global management plane: the distributed control plane behind on-demand and reserved clusters across dozens of data centers, including the systems that scale per-cluster limits and automate the onboarding of new capacity.

  • Set the engineering bar: create the testing frameworks, tools, and developer documentation that make our systems robust and usable by other teams, and shape the core, open-source Together AI platform.

We are looking for an LLM Engineer to design, execute, and operationalize fine-tuning workflows for large language models across supervised, preference-based, and reinforcement learning approaches. The role requires deep practical experience with modern training stacks, careful dataset construction, rigorous evaluation methodology, and the engineering discipline to operate complex training pipelines reliably. jobs.title: Data Scientist, Project Success and Innovation
jobs.description:
AIR is seeking a Data Scientist to join the Project Success and Innovation (PSI) team and the Employment and Economic Opportunity Program (EEOP), providing advanced technical expertise to support innovation development, scaling efforts, and applied research and analytics across project teams. Within PSI, the Data Scientist will contribute to AIR’s Innovation Lab by co-designing, developing, and scaling solutions that strengthen and amplify effective practices across diverse technical and operational workflows.

Within EEOP, the Data Scientist will lead end-to-end quantitative workflows, including establishing and maintaining reproducible analytic environments, managing and quality assuring complex datasets, reviewing and strengthening junior staff members’ code, and conducting advanced statistical analyses. These analyses may include causal approaches, such as experimental and quasi-experimental designs, as well as non-causal approaches, including descriptive, predictive, and explanatory modeling. The Data Scientist will also help expand AIR’s capacity to responsibly apply machine learning methods in support of both research and operational objectives, while translating technical findings into clear, actionable products for clients, partners, and other stakeholders.

Candidates hired for the position may work remotely within the United States (U.S.) or from one of our U.S. office locations. This does not include U.S. territories.
About AIR:

Founded in 1946 and headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, the American Institutes for Research (AIR) is a nonpartisan, not-for-profit organization that conducts behavioral and social science research and delivers technical assistance to address some of the most pressing challenges in the United States and globally. We generate evidence and apply data-driven solutions that expand opportunities and improve lives for all.
Responsibilities

The responsibilities for the position include:

PSI (approximately 50%)
• Build and maintain shared analytic tools, including code libraries, project templates, and pipelines, that research teams across AIR can adopt and reuse.
• Write documentation, training materials, and onboarding guides that make modern tooling accessible to staff with varying levels of technical experience.
• Support project teams adopting new tools and workflows by answering questions, troubleshooting, and relaying recurring problems back to the team.
• Prototype and test new tools and platforms, including machine learning and AI applications such as large language models, and help assess their fit and responsible use at AIR.
• Help maintain deployed tools by triaging issues, fixing bugs, and tracking user feedback.
• Contribute to work plans, timelines, and progress tracking for PSI activities, communicating regularly with PSI leadership.

EEOP (approximately 50%)
• Conduct quantitative analyses on research and evaluation projects, including analyses for causal and non-causal research questions.
• Serve as lead analyst on discrete studies or analytic components, with support from senior researchers.
• Manage, clean, and quality-assure complex datasets from multiple sources.
• Build and document reproducible analytic workflows and quality control procedures.
• Review analytic code produced by research associates and other junior staff, and support their development in reproducible analysis and documentation practices.
• Contribute to study design and analytic planning discussions.
• Draft analytic sections of client reports, technical memos, and presentations, and help translate findings for non-technical audiences.
• Track deliverables and timelines for assigned analytic tasks.
• Contribute technical content to proposals.
Qualifications:

Education, Knowledge, and Experience
• Master's or doctoral degree in a quantitative field, including statistics, computational social science, education data science, statistics, economics, quantitative psychology, quantitative methods, data scien

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As an Applied AI Engineer on the Startups team at Anthropic, you will be a trusted technical advisor to the top AI-native startups building in the physical world, across robotics, semiconductors, aerospace, manufacturing, and civil infrastructure, as they grow from early product to scale. Some of these companies build the hardware itself and want Claude woven into how they design, test, and operate it, and others build the software that engineers everywhere use to design, simulate, test, and scale, and this role works with both. You'll lead deep technical engagements, partnering directly with startup software and hardware engineering teams to help them build their products on Claude and run their own engineering with it, advising on implementation and agent design as they build what is newly possible with AI in the physical world. At LangChain, our mission is to make intelligent agents ubiquitous. We build the foundation for agent engineering in the real world, helping developers move from prototypes to production-ready AI agents that teams can rely on. We began as widely adopted open-source tools and have grown to also offer a platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating agents at scale.

With $125M raised at Series B from IVP, Sequoia, Benchmark, CapitalG, and Sapphire Ventures, we’re at a stage where we’re continuing to develop new products, growth is accelerating, and all team members have meaningful impact on what we build and how we work together. LangChain is a place where your contributions can shape how this technology shows up in the real world.

Today, our platform includes LangSmith (Observability, Evaluation, Deployment, Fleet, and Sandboxes), our open source frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents), and the newly launched LangSmith Engine for autonomous agent improvement. We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater.

LangChain is looking for a GTM Enablement Program Manager to help keep our growing go-to-market organization informed, enabled, and ready to execute as our products and company evolve.

We operate in one of the fastest-moving areas of technology. Our products evolve quickly, new capabilities launch frequently, and the knowledge our GTM teams rely on is constantly changing. As we scale, we need a strong operating system that ensures sellers understand what we're building, why it matters, how to talk about it, and where to find the information they need.

This role will own three critical areas of our enablement engine: Product Enablement, GTM Knowledge & Content, and Enablement Communications.

You'll partner closely with Product, Engineering, Product Marketing, Sales, and Revenue Operations to turn product changes and company knowledge into scalable training, resources, communications, and systems for GTM.

Working with cross funtional subject matter experts, your job is to turn messaging, trainings, and artifacts into field readiness—making sure GTM can learn it, find it, understand it, and use it.

 - Own the product enablement engine. Stay closely connected to Product, Engineering, and Product Marketing to understand what's changing, determine the impact to GTM, and partner with these SMEs to build practical field enablement.

 - Own GTM readiness for product launches and major changes. Build the enablement plan from initial intake through launch, including training, communications, resource publication, reinforcement, and ongoing maintenance.

 - Build and maintain product training. Create and continuously improve product curriculum in our LMS and Content Hub so sellers have a clear learning path across our platform, products, use cases, positioning, and value.

 - Run live product enablement. Determine when asynchronous learning isn't enough, coordinate the right SMEs, and facilitate live sessions, workshops, demos, and deeper product training.

 - Measure readiness and close gaps. Use feedback, participation, knowledge checks, field questions, and other signals to understand where GTM needs additional reinforcement.

jobs.title: Senior / Staff Security Engineer
jobs.description:
At Linear, we're building the product development system for teams and agents. AI is fundamentally changing how software gets built, and we’re shaping the tools this new era requires.

Founded in 2019, Linear has become the platform of choice for more than 30,000 companies (including OpenAI, Coinbase, and Ramp) to plan, build, and ship their products. Today, our team is distributed across North America, Europe, and Australia, and we’re continuing to grow internationally. What unites us is relentless focus, fast execution, and a deep care for software craftsmanship.

At Linear, we are committed to quality. Security is an essential part of that quality — not a layer that we add later, but something we build in from the start. We have a foundational security program we're proud of but, as Linear evolves our product and scales into enterprise, there's meaningful work ahead: staying ahead of vulnerabilities as our attack surface grows, responding fast and cleanly when incidents happen, and hardening our product and infrastructure. As Security Engineer at Linear, you'll be operating in a high-autonomy role with real scope, doing hands-on security work across the product and infrastructure we build.

Location & work mode

Linear is a remote-first company. This role is open to candidates based in North America. You can work from anywhere within this region. We value deep focus and async collaboration, with intentional moments to connect in person through team off-sites, optional co-working, and occasional travel.

What you’ll do

Depending on your experience / skillset and our broader priorities, you could:

 - Operate, automate, and extend vulnerability management end-to-end: triage, prioritize, and drive remediation across product, infrastructure, and dependencies, and keep the program’s SLAs meaningful rather than theoretical

 - Run our bug bounty program: triage incoming reports, validate severity, work with engineering on fixes, and keep researcher relationships professional and responsive

 - Lead product security testing: threat model new features (including AI/agent-facing surfaces), review designs and code for security-relevant risk, and do hands-on testing (manual and tool-assisted) rather than relying solely on scanners

 - Be a primary responder for security incidents: lead investigation and containment, drive postmortems, and turn lessons into concrete hardening work

 - Own meaningful chunks of our cloud/infra security posture on GCP/k8s/Postgres: harden configurations, close gaps surfaced by audits or scanning, and partner with infra engineering on secure defaults

 - Build and maintain security tooling and automation, including using AI/LLM tooling to speed up triage, code review, and repetitive investigation work, so the program scales without linear headcount growth

 - Partner with the GRC/Trust function: feed real findings into the risk register and control evidence, and help make sure compliance requirements reflect actual engineering practice

What we’re looking for

 - A generalist, senior-level security engineer (5+ years across security engineering, with real depth in at least two of: vulnerability management, product/appsec testing, incident response, and cloud security). We need breadth, rather than a narrow specialist in any one of these.

 - Hands-on and technical: you can read and reason about code (we use a lot of TypeScript), you’re comfortable in cloud environments (GCP a plus), and you can go deep on a finding rather than just filing a ticket for someone else to fix. You’re comfortable using AI coding/security tools as force multipliers (Linear Agent, Claude, Codex, etc).

 - Calm under pressure: you can lead an incident from first alert through postmortem without needing to be told what to do next

 - A builder: you’d rather write a script or ship a tool than repeat a manual process a third time

 - A pragmatic risk-reducer: you optimize for actually reducing risk, not for checking a box or maximizi

Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

SpaceXSI is building Colossus, the world’s largest AI supercomputer, right here in Memphis. As a Power Generation Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in powering this groundbreaking infrastructure. You will be responsible for the reliable operation and optimization of our natural gas power generation plants, ensuring uninterrupted, high-efficiency power delivery to our state-of-the-art AI datacenter. This is an opportunity to work at the intersection of energy engineering and cutting-edge AI technology, contributing to advancements that push the boundaries of human knowledge. If you thrive in a dynamic, high-stakes environment where your expertise directly impacts global innovation, this role is for you.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Oversee the daily operations of natural gas turbines and associated power generation equipment, ensuring optimal performance and compliance with safety and environmental standards.
  • Monitor and analyze power generation systems to detect and resolve issues proactively, minimizing downtime and maximizing efficiency for the datacenter's massive computational demands.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including electrical engineers and datacenter operations, to integrate power systems seamlessly with AI infrastructure needs.
  • Conduct regular maintenance, troubleshooting, and upgrades on turbines, generators, and control systems to support scalable power requirements.
  • Develop and implement strategies for energy efficiency, cost reduction, and sustainable power generation practices.
  • Lead root cause analysis for any power-related incidents and drive continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Ensure all operations adhere to regulatory requirements, including those from local, state, and federal agencies governing natural gas plants.
  • Mentor junior engineers and technicians, fostering a culture of excellence and innovation in power management.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or a related field.
  • 1+ years of experience in power generation, with a focus on natural gas plants, turbines, or similar high-reliability energy systems.
  • Strong understanding of turbine operations, control systems, and power distribution in industrial settings.
  • Proven track record in troubleshooting complex mechanical and electrical issues in power generation environments.
  • Familiarity with safety protocols, environmental regulations, and industry standards (e.g., ASME, IEEE).

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Master's degree in a relevant engineering discipline.
  • 5+ years of experience, including leadership roles in power plant operations or datacenter energy management.
  • Expertise in natural gas turbine technologies (e.g., GE, Siemens) and combined cycle power plants.
  • Knowledge of renewable energy integration or hybrid power systems.</

jobs.title: Lead Technical Enablement Specialist, Field Capability & Readiness
jobs.description:
SLSQ227R703

About the Role

The Field Engineering role is changing quickly. AI is changing how technical work gets done, products and customer needs are evolving faster, and the capabilities that distinguish an exceptional FE today will not be exactly the same ones that matter tomorrow.

Databricks is looking for a Lead Technical Enablement Specialist to help define and build the capability engine for our global Field Engineering organization. You will shape how FEs build expertise, demonstrate readiness, share what they know, and apply their capabilities with customers.

This role owns a portfolio, not a single program. That portfolio may include skills verification, technical validation, role-based readiness paths, practical challenges, and new approaches we have not yet imagined. Your job is to understand where the field is headed, identify the capabilities that will matter most, and turn that insight into experiences and systems that help FEs grow and perform.

This is a high-visibility, high-autonomy role for someone who wants to build. You will work with FE leaders, product and technical communities, regional teams, enablement partners, HR, and internal platform teams to define what “field-ready” means and make it useful in the flow of work. You will have the opportunity to influence how a global technical organization develops - and to create programs that become part of how Databricks operates.

The best person for this role is equal parts strategist, product thinker, builder, and operator. You can see around corners, create structure from ambiguity, earn trust with senior stakeholders, and turn an idea into something the field actually uses. You are energized by the possibility of using AI not only as a topic to teach, but as a catalyst to redesign how capability is built, measured, and scaled.

What You'll Do

  • Set the vision and roadmap for FE capability. Develop a clear point of view on how Databricks should build, demonstrate, recognize, and continuously evolve field expertise. Translate FE strategy, product priorities, customer needs, and the changing nature of technical work into a focused portfolio of investments.
  • Own and evolve a portfolio of readiness experiences. Bring together existing programs and new opportunities across skills verification, technical demonstrations, role-based pathways, credentials, and practical application. Decide what to scale, redesign, connect, or retire to keep the portfolio coherent and valuable.
  • Invent new ways for FEs to build and prove expertise. When the field needs a new capability, design the right experience - not automatically another course. This could be a customer scenario, a live technical demonstration, a peer review, a contribution model, an AI-enabled assessment, or something entirely new. Prototype quickly, learn from the field, and scale the strongest ideas.
  • Make readiness relevant to the work FEs actually do. Partner with practitioners, managers, product teams, and SME communities to define credible standards and evidence of capability. Embed development and validation into existing FE workflows wherever possible, making readiness a pull-based experience rather than an additional layer of process.
  • Help the organization adapt to an AI-enabled future. Stay close to how AI is changing FE workflows, technical depth, customer engagement, and delivery models. Ensure our capability models measure judgment, problem-solving, architecture, collaboration, and customer impact - not just static product knowledge. Experiment with AI to improve assessment quality, personalize development, surface expertise, and scale program operations responsibly.
  • Create the systems and signals that make capability visible. Partner with internal platform and engineer

jobs.title: Principal Kernel & Device Drivers Engineer
jobs.description:
SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

About the role
 SambaNova is seeking a Principal Engineer to own kernel-level drivers and low-level software for high-speed IO, memory, and networking subsystems within the DataScale® platform and RDU architecture. This role is central to delivering reliable, high-performance AI systems at scale. This is a hands-on Linux kernel and device driver role; it is not an application or platform software role.

You will lead software bring-up of new silicon, deliver production drivers across the IO, memory, and network data paths, and debug complex issues spanning kernel, firmware, and hardware. This role suits an engineer with deep kernel and driver expertise and strong hardware fluency, who can operate in ambiguity and execute with high ownership.

Responsibilities

  • Own kernel-space drivers for high-speed IO, memory, and networking subsystems, from architecture through production release
  • Own the RDMA and network data path, including queue-pair management, congestion control, QoS, and packet classification
  • Lead software enablement for platform bring-up across new silicon and system configurations
  • Drive issues to root cause across kernel, firmware, and hardware layers with hardware, firmware, and validation teams
  • Own PHY and link bring-up in coordination with hardware teams, working from specifications and register documentation
  • Build tools, test scripts, and frameworks for device and NIC verification, performance analysis, and manufacturing test
  • Identify and resolve bottlenecks across driver, network stack, and system layers at data center scale
  • Set code quality standards through design and code review, and mentor engineers on the team

Required Qualifications

  • MS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field
  • 7+ years of experience in kernel or low-level system software development
  • Deep expertise in Linux systems programming and kernel driver development
  • Strong knowledge of Linux kernel networking, including network driver development and the RDMA protocol
  • Strong C/C++ programming and debugging skills, with scripting in Python or shell
  • Experience with two or more high-speed IO or interconnect technologies such as PCIe, Ethernet, or CXL
  • Proven ability to lead hardware-software co-debug from first silicon to production
  • Ability to read and distill hardware specifications and register-level documentation
  • Clear and effective communicator with a proactive, collaborative approach to problem-solving

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on RDMA data-path or driver implementation experience
  • Experience with virtual switching and data center networking at scale
  • Experience writing test scripts to verify NIC behavior
  • Firmware development experience
  • Exposure to pre-silicon validation using FPGA or emulation platforms
  • Background in high-performance computing or accelerator-based systems

jobs.title: Lead Solutions Architect - Generative AI (EMEA Emerging DNB)
jobs.description:
REQ ID: FEQ227R147

Location: Germany (Remote/Hybrid) - will require travel across Europe

Recruiter: Dina Hussain

About the Role

We are looking for a Lead Solution Architect focused on Generative AI to support our EMEA Emerging Digital Natives and Startups business unit — one of the fastest-moving, most technically ambitious patches in EMEA. Our customers are digital-native and cloud-native companies who build on the frontier: they adopt GenAI early, scale fast, and expect their technical partners to be as sharp as their own engineers.

You will be the go-to expert our Account Teams and customers turn to when a GenAI or LLM use case needs to move from an ambitious idea to a production-grade reality across our high-growth accounts.

This is a highly technical, customer-facing individual contributor role for someone who lives at the frontier of applied GenAI. You will shape architectures, prove out the hard problems, challenge and influence customer roadmaps, and raise the GenAI capability of the entire EMEA Emerging DNB field organisation.

What You'll Do

  • Serve as the deep technical authority on Generative AI, LLMs, and applied machine learning for the EMEA Emerging DNB business unit, supporting the most strategic and complex customer engagements across our digital-native and born-in-the-cloud accounts.
  • Partner with our EMEA Emerging DNB Solutions Architects, Solutions Engineers, and Account teams to scope, design, and de-risk GenAI use cases — from retrieval-augmented generation and agentic systems to fine-tuning and evaluation.
  • Build hands-on proofs of concept and reference implementations that operationalise large-scale LLM and deep learning workloads on Databricks (Mosaic AI, MLflow, Model Serving, Vector Search, Unity Catalog governance), tuned to the fast iteration cycles Emerging DNB customers expect.
  • Lead fine-tuning and model-customisation engagements on open LLMs (e.g., Llama-family models), including judge-based and label-efficient evaluation approaches for domains where quality and safety are paramount.
  • Act as a bridge to Product and Engineering — channel field and customer feedback into the roadmap and represent the roadmap back to the field.
  • Enable and mentor the broader EMEA Emerging DNB Field Engineering team through workshops, reference architectures, and internal enablement, multiplying GenAI expertise across our ~70-person SA/SE organisation.
  • Represent Databricks externally as a technical thought leader — conference talks (e.g., Data + AI Summit), blogs, and customer executive briefings.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong understanding of the LLM landscape, including leading proprietary and open-source models and providers, with the ability to differentiate their capabilities, trade-offs, and suitability for different use cases, and to articulate a clear, informed point of view (POV) to customers.
  • Deep expertise in the modern GenAI stack: LLM application patterns (RAG, agents, tool use), fine-tuning and model customization, prompt and evaluation engineering, and LLM guardrails/safety.
  • Strong foundations in machine learning and deep learning, including distributed training, GPU workloads, and the full MLOps lifecycle (tracking, registry, serving, monitoring).
  • Proficiency in Python and the ML ecosystem (PyTorch/Transformers, MLflow, Spark), and comfort building production-quality reference implementations.
  • Experience with the Databricks platform — or the ability to ramp on it quickly — including Mosaic AI, Model Serving, Vector Search, and Unity Catalog. Cloud experience across AWS, Azure, or GCP.
  • Excellent communication and consultative skills: able to earn the trust of both hands-on engineers and senior tech

jobs.title: Delivery Solutions Architect - High-Tech & Manufacturing
jobs.description:
CSQ427R106

At Databricks, we are on a mission to empower our customers to solve the world's toughest data problems by utilizing the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform. As a Delivery Solutions Architect (DSA), you will play an important role during this journey. You will collaborate with our sales and field engineering teams to accelerate the adoption and growth of the Databricks platform in your customers. You will also help ensure customer success by increasing focus and technical accountability for our most complex customers who need guidance to accelerate usage of Databricks workloads they have already selected, helping them maximize the value they get from our platform and their return on investment.

This is a hybrid technical and commercial role. It is commercial in the sense that you will drive growth in your assigned customers and use cases through leading your customers' stakeholders, building executive relationships, orchestrating other focused/specialized teams within Databricks, and creating and driving plans and strategies for Databricks colleagues to build upon. This is in parallel to being technical, with the expectation that you will become the post-sale technical lead across all Databricks products. This requires you to use your skills and technical credibility to engage and communicate effectively with an organization at all levels. You will report directly to a DSA Manager within the Field Engineering organization. 

The impact you will have:

  • Engage with Solutions Architects to understand the full use case demand plan for prioritized customers
  • Lead the post-technical win technical account strategy and execution plan for the majority of Databricks use cases within our most strategic accounts
  • Be the accountable technical leader assigned to specific use cases and customer(s) across multiple selling teams and internal stakeholders, creating certainty from uncertainty and driving onboarding, enablement, success, go-live, and healthy consumption of the workloads where the customer has made the decision to consume Databricks
  • Be the first contact for any technical issues or questions related to the production/go-live status of agreed-upon use cases within an account, oftentimes services multiple use cases within the largest and most complex organizations
  • Leverage both Shared Services, User Education, Onboarding/Technical Services, and Support resources, along with escalating to expert-level technical experts, to build the right tasks that are beyond your scope of activities or expertise
  • Create, own, and execute a point of view as to how key use cases can be accelerated into production, coordinating with Professional Services (PS) resources on the delivery of PS Engagement proposals
  • Navigate Databricks Product and Engineering teams for new product Innovations, private previews, and upgrade needs
  • Develop an execution plan that covers all activities of all customer-facing technical roles and teams to cover the following work streams:
    • Main use cases moving from ‘win’ to production
    • Enablement/user growth plan
    • Product adoption (strategy and activities to increase adoption of Databricks’ Lakehouse vision)
    • Organic needs for current investment (e.g. cloud cost control, tuning & optimization)
    • Executive and operational governance
  • Provide internal and external updates - KPI reporting on the status of usage and customer health, covering investment status, important risks, product adoption and use case progression - to your Technical GM

What we look for:

  • 5+ years of experience where you have been accountable for technical project/program delivery within the domain of Data and AI, and where you can contribute to technical debate and design choices with customers
  • Progr

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Fleet Platform
jobs.description:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING ADVANCED AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and into the real world. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. Today, we're deploying autonomous systems on heavy construction equipment across the country, improving safety on job sites and accelerating schedules on critical infrastructure projects.

We're not here debating the future of AI. We're deploying it in the real world. In just two years, we've raised $350M and achieved the first fully autonomous excavator deployments in construction.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As Bedrock scales deployments nationwide, every machine we bring autonomy to has to be vetted, provisioned, calibrated, deployed, monitored, updated and serviced. Fleet Engineering builds the platform behind that lifecycle: the system of record, services and applications that teams across Bedrock use to run a fleet growing to thousands of machines. Many of these systems will be used by external partners as well.



The work crosses disciplines. One week you're architecting how we track sensor calibrations across every machine. The next, you're making a fault on an operator's tablet readable at a glance. You'll own problems end to end, working closely with technicians and operators in the field as well as multidisciplinary engineers across hardware, ML and robotics.



Also, you get to drive 100,000 lb excavators.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the fleet system of record: the data model and services for machines, their hardware, worksites and deployments, and how each moves through its lifecycle

 - Build the applications that technicians, dispatchers and operations teams use every day to vet machines, schedule installs, track inventory and keep the fleet healthy

 - Build the services every robot phones home to: delivering identity, credentials, calibrations and configuration to machines in the field, and always knowing what's running where

 - Move petabytes of sensor data off remote job sites across the country, bringing home the real-world data that powers our ML and learning flywheel

 - Spend real time with the people who use what you build, in the office and in the field, and turn messy real-world workflows into simple, durable software

 - Design foundational APIs that other engineering teams and external partners build on, and evolve them safely as the business changes

 - Lean into AI and agents, from automating development workflows to fleet triage and operations
   
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years building and shipping production software, owning systems from design through operation

jobs.description:
SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

About the role

Sambanova is looking for a talented and motivated Principal Design for Test (DFT) Engineer to help us build state-of-the-art RDU chips for machine learning and artificial intelligence. We are looking for a highly hands-on engineer who will be responsible for DFT architecture and implementation, verification, ATPG, MBIST and silicon bring-up for complex high-performance chips

Responsibilities

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Define & implement block-level and SoC-level DFT architecture for large, hierarchical SoCs
  • Develop and maintain ATPG flows for stuck-at,  at-speed and advanced fault models.
  • Develop scripts and automation for DFT insertion, ATPG, coverage analysis, pattern generation, and debug.
  • Develop and maintain JTAG, IEEE 1500, and IEEE 1687/IJTAG infrastructure for internal test and debug access.
  • Generate production-quality ATPG and MBIST patterns and support deployment to ATE.
  • Work closely with STA and Physical Design teams on DFT timing closure
  • Support silicon diagnosis, failure localization, yield analysis, and manufacturing test optimization.

Required Qualifications

  • B.S. in computer science, computer engineering, or related field
  • 10+ years relevant industry experience
  • Deep understanding of scan insertion, scan compression, ATPG, MBIST, JTAG, and hierarchical DFT
  • Hands-on experience with Siemens Tessent tool flow (preferred) or equivalent industry standard DFT tools
  • Familiarity with cell-aware ATPG, small-delay defects, IEEE 1500, IEEE 1687/IJTAG, and low-power DFT is highly desirable
  • Strong understanding of advanced ATPG, silicon diagnosis, and failure localization methodologies
  • Experience with STA constraints & analysis for DFT modes & SDF simulations
  • Working knowledge of Verilog/System-Verilog simulators & waveform debugging

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with ATE pattern deployment and silicon bring-up 
  • Experience with multi-die/chiplet DFT, known-good-die test, or die-to-die interface testing
  • Experience with large compute, AI accelerator, or HPC SoCs

$180,000—$255,000 USD

About the role

Anthropic is seeking a Director, Infrastructure Lease Accounting to lead technical accounting for our most complex infrastructure and energy arrangements — the data center leases and related structures underpinning our recently significant investment in American computing infrastructure. As we continue our rapid growth, you will ensure the financial statement accuracy of the most technically complex contracts we enter into.

This is an opportunity to be at the heart of one of the fastest-scaling companies in the industry, and to shape how Anthropic accounts for the highest-stakes arrangements underpinning our compute and energy portfolio.

You will serve as the technical accounting subject matter expert for arrangements spanning data center leases (ASC 842), and counterparty or joint-venture structures (ASC 810 VIE analysis). You'll work closely with Real Estate, Legal, Finance, and external auditors to ensure accounting implications are understood before commitments are made.

  • Apply ASC 842 to complex lease arrangements, including lease identification, modifications, reassessments, and embedded leases within compute, colocation, and data center contracts

  • Apply ASC 810 to counterparty and joint-venture structures, including variable interest entity (VIE) analysis for special purpose entities

  • Apply ASC 815 to energy and infrastructure arrangements, including consideration of embedded derivatives

  • Lead technical accounting analysis and memo preparation for new arrangements, ensuring positions are well-reasoned, supported, and auditor-ready

  • Partner with Real Estate, Legal, and Finance teams during contract negotiation and execution to ensure accounting implications are understood before commitments are made

  • Serve as a trusted finance partner to non-finance stakeholders — explaining the financial statement impact of their decisions in clear, simple terms they can act on

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff - Storage (Stockholm)
jobs.description:
ABOUT US:
AI NEEDS A NEW INFRASTRUCTURE LAYER. WE'RE BUILDING IT AT MODAL.

Every era of computing brought new workloads that previous infrastructure couldn't support: mainframes, databases, and the cloud. Each time, the company that rebuilt the layer underneath defined the decade. AI is no different, except it touches everything instead of one slice, and the window to build the layer underneath it is open right now.


Our customers include category-defining companies like Ramp https://modal.com/blog/how-ramp-built-a-full-context-background-coding-agent-on-modal, Cognition, DoorDash, and Suno. They rely on Modal for instant GPU access, sub-second container starts, and native storage, so it's simple to serve low-latency inference, fine-tune models, and access production-ready sandboxes at scale.


We've passed $1B in annualized run rate, up 15x from a year ago. In October 2026 we raised a $750M Series D led by Accel at a $15.75B valuation.


Our team includes creators of popular open-source projects (e.g.,Seaborn https://github.com/mwaskom/seaborn,Luigi https://github.com/spotify/luigi), academic researchers, international olympiad medalists, and experienced engineering and product leaders with decades of experience.




THE ROLE:

We are looking for strong engineers with experience and interest in designing, building, and maintaining the novel, high-performance systems that make up our serverless platform. Specifically, you'll be working on the distributed object storage system that underpins every container image, volume, and checkpoint on Modal: hundreds of petabytes of data, replicated across multiple cloud object stores and a CDN, cached on local NVMe across a large fleet of workers in many datacenters, and shared peer-to-peer within each datacenter. You'll make cold starts feel local when the data is hundreds of milliseconds away, designing the caching, preloading, and peer-to-peer layers that hide object-store latency and keep public ingress off saturated uplinks. You'll own durability and cost at petabyte scale, from streaming and batch replication between origins, to garbage collection over billions of objects. You'll work across the stack, from local disk and page cache to distributed blob storage and garbage collection and you'll help shape what storage becomes next as we push storage closer to workloads.



REQUIREMENTS:

 - 5+ years of experience writing high-quality production code

 - Experience building high-performance distributed storage or caching systems at a large scale (the more challenges you've worked through, the better)

 - Strong cloud skills, including deep familiarity with object storage (S3 or similar), CDNs, and their consistency, throughput, and cost characteristics

 - Strong knowledge of low-level operating system foundations (Linux kernel, file systems, page cache, containers, etc.)

 - Willingness to step into the thick of it with our on-call rotation and respond to production incidents
   


NICE-TO-HAVES:

 - Experience with replication, content addressing, and consistency models in multi-region or multi-cloud systems

 - Experience operating storage systems at scale (petabyte-scale datasets, high-throughput read/write paths, large-scale garbage collection or data migration)

 - Experience with data engineering at petabyte-scale.

 - Prior experience with Rust
   


KEY THINGS THE TEAM IS WORKING ON:

 - P2P sharing of data across workers within a single datacenter to dramatically reduce ingress

 - Replicating data across multiple blob storage providers

 - Automating garbage collection across hundreds of petabytes of data

 - Deploying colocated storage clusters to datacenters to accelerate high-throughput customer workloads

jobs.description:
Bedrock Robotics, Inc. seeks a Hardware Engineer in San Francisco, CA responsible for designing, manufacturing, and testing its autonomous hardware systems, including high performance computer systems, sensors, controllers, interfaces to machines, and testing equipment.

This position will work with autonomous hardware systems installed on standard heavy construction machinery—excavators, bulldozers, and wheel loaders—to allow that equipment to perform earthmoving work on construction sites autonomously. In this context, “autonomous hardware systems” are the physical electronic components installed on a construction machine that allow it to operate without a human operator in the cab. They consist of: high-performance computer systems (ruggedized onboard computers mounted on the machine that perform the calculations required for autonomous operation); sensors (devices that allow the machine to perceive its surroundings, including cameras, radar, lidar, and GNSS); controllers and interfaces (electronic units that translate the computer's decisions into electrical signals that operate the machine's existing hydraulic, steering, and engine controls); and testing equipment (benches, fixtures, and instrumentation used to verify each of the above components before and after installation on a machine). Working together, these systems continuously collect sensor data, determine the machine's position and what is around it, calculate the path the machine should follow and the movements it should make, and then command the machine's controls to carry out those movements, performing the tasks a human operator would otherwise perform manually.

Specific duties include: (i) defining and designing hardware systems, including component-level architecture for autonomous machines and camera/optics design and performance; (ii) establishing and leading relationships and programs with external vendors to facilitate hardware manufacturing and delivery; (iii) supporting hardware system verification and validation, including working with safety teams to establish/tune requirements and performance metrics for components and systems; (iv) using industry standard tools and knowledge to test standards of hardware systems; and (v) writing reusable, high quality sensor data analysis and testing automation software.

This is a hybrid office-based/work-from-home position within the United States. The employee can work remotely from within the United States but must be able to work in the San Francisco office at least three (3) days per week.

Must have a bachelor’s degree (or foreign equivalent) in Electrical Engineering, Robotics Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a directly related field plus five (5) years of progressively responsible, post-baccalaureate experience in designing, integrating, and validating electrical hardware systems.

Must have any experience with: (i) high performance computer systems, including x86 or ARM; (ii) robotics sensors stacks, including lidar, radar, camera, or GNSS; (iii) communication protocols and technologies, including CAN, LIN, J1939, FlexRay, or Ethernet; (iv) python or C++/C/Rust; and (v) standardization tools and organizations, including ISO, SAE, and ANSI.

Must be willing and able to travel regionally/nationally up to 15%, to visit hardware testing sites.

Experience can be concurrent.

This position is expected to pay an annual salary of $236,000.

Apply online at bedrockrobotics.com/careers http://bedrockrobotics.com/careers.

jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.


ABOUT THE ROLE

You embed directly with customer teams as the engineer on the ground: own an outcome, ship a production-grade SpaceXSI system that still runs after you leave, and become the critical technical feedback loop from the field back to product engineering.

The work is the project. One week you might take a messy business workflow and put a production agent on it: pick the use case, stand up the architecture, wire it into the customer’s auth, data, and tools, then harden it with evals until the team actually uses it. Another week you might live in a customer’s repo and delivery system and ship an agent-powered path for a migration, a PR review loop, or an incident-to-fix flow, behind tests, review, and rollout rather than in a chat sidebar. Either way, you measure what matters, leave the customer able to operate it, and bring the pattern back as another use case for SpaceXAI.

This is not a demo role. You own the work end to end, from the first discovery call through launch, iteration, and post-launch support, and you are responsible for systems that work in the real world.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Lead discovery with the customer: orient in their codebases and workflows, find the real bottleneck and the use case worth building, and define clear success metrics

 - Design and ship production agents, AI applications, and coding-agent workflows on Grok and our models, on live business processes and inside the customer’s engineering org

 - Get a first version live in days, then harden it over weeks with rollout, monitoring, and iteration from real usage

 - Own production quality: tracing, evals, debugging model or delivery failures, and latency and cost tradeoffs

 - Build the systems around the model (tools, MCP servers, retrieval, rules, skills, CI gates, and evals) and integrate them into the customer’s auth, data, workflow, and delivery systems; decide when prompting, architecture, data, process, or a model change is the right lever

 - Measure the outcome that matters (revenue, cost, hours saved, error rate, cycle time, escaped defects), not seat adoption

 - Work directly with Staff+, platform, and domain leaders, going deep in their systems while communicating clearly about tradeoffs and results

 - Leave the customer team able to run what you built, and turn what you learn into reusable patterns and improvements to SpaceXAI products




YOU MAY BE A FIT IF

   - You’ve owned a customer or operator outcome, not just a slide or a prototype, and can turn a fuzzy problem into a scoped, shipped system
   
   - You’ve built and owned AI-native workflows or agents in production, and debugged real production failures (model, tool, data, pipeline, or delivery path)

Why this role exists

TNS is moving from AI governance and foundations into execution. The platform building blocks are in place or underway — Microsoft 365, Copilot, Entra ID, SharePoint, and Anthropic's Claude models via AWS Bedrock. What we don't yet have is a dedicated person who can both build and operate the secure, production-grade AI platform that lets AI work safely against our data and embed with our lines of business to turn that capability into measurable value.

This role does both. You'll be the technical engine and the on-the-ground partner who makes AI a productive, trusted tool across the enterprise — and who multiplies that impact by enabling others to build, not just building yourself.

What You'll Do

Your time will span two connected halves.

Build and operate the AI platform

Model platform and private hosting. Own our Claude deployment on AWS Bedrock end to end — model access and versioning, region and data-residency decisions, provisioned throughput vs. on-demand, and the private, VPC-isolated hosting posture that keeps our data inside our boundary and out of third-party training. Data connectivity. Design and build secure, governed connections between AI systems and TNS data — Microsoft 365 and Graph, SharePoint, databases, data warehouses, APIs, and line-of-business systems. Own the retrieval architecture, indexing and freshness strategy, and the permission-trimming that ensures every user sees only what they're entitled to see, with no leakage across boundaries.

Security and access control. Cost management. Job Description Summary
Organization's Summary Statement:
The Applied Research Laboratory for Intelligence & Security (ARLIS) at the University of Maryland is a University-Affiliated Research Center (UARC) dedicated to advancing research, innovation, and technology transition to improve decision making for U.S. national security. ARLIS combines deep scientific expertise with operational insight to address challenges in intelligence analysis, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence / machine learning, quantum science, and human-machine teaming. Researchers, scientists, engineers, and analysts at ARLIS collaborate with government agencies, industry partners, and academic institutions to deliver actionable insights and transformative solutions through research and development. Employees at ARLIS work on projects of critical importance, contribute directly to the nation’s security, and are supported by a culture that values integrity, collaboration, and professional growth.

ARLIS is seeking a mid-level MLOps Engineer to support the deployment, scaling, and operationalization of machine learning systems for national security applications. This role focuses on bridging research and production by enabling robust, secure, and reproducible ML pipelines in mission-critical environments. The successful candidate will work closely with AI researchers, software engineers, and domain experts to transition advanced algorithms into operational capabilities.

Key Responsibilities:
-Design, build, and maintain scalable ML pipelines for training, evaluation, and deployment.
-Operationalize machine learning models in secure, production-grade environments (on-prem, cloud, hybrid).
-Implement CI/CD workflows for ML systems, including automated testing, validation, and monitoring.
-Manage data pipelines, feature stores, and model versioning to ensure reproducibility and auditability.
-Monitor model performance, drift, and system health; implement feedback loops and retraining strategies.
-Collaborate with researchers to translate experimental models into production-ready systems.
-Integrate security best practices into ML workflows (DevSecOps for AI systems).
-Support deployment of ML systems in constrained or classified environments.
-Contribute to infrastructure design supporting AI/ML workloads (GPU clusters, distributed systems).

Must be able to obtain a U.S. security clearance. If selected, you must meet the requirements for access to classified information and will be subject to a government security clearance investigation that includes criminal and credit history checks, as well as verification of U.S. citizenship, birth, education, employment, and military history.

Final offer is contingent upon the candidate’s ability to successfully obtain the necessary interim Secret security clearance, as determined by the U.S. Government, prior to commencing employment.

Physical Demands:
Sedentary work performed in a normal office environment; exerts up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and/or negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects, including the human body. Ability to attend meetings both on and off campus. Spending long hours in front of a computer screen.

Minimum Qualifications:
-Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or related field.
-3–6 years of experience in software engineering, data engineering, or MLOps.
-Experience with ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) and pipeline tools (e.g., Airflow, Kubeflow).
-Proficiency in Python and experience with containerization (Docker) and orchestration (Kubernetes).
-Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and ML services.
-Understanding of software engineering best practices (CI/CD, testing, version control).

Preferences:
-Experience deploying ML systems in regulated or security-sensitive environments.
-Familiarity with data governance, model auditing, and explainability techniques.

jobs.title: Edge AI Engineer
jobs.description:
Edge AI Engineer – Remote

Bright Vision Technologies is a technology consulting and software development company delivering cloud, AI, data, and enterprise solutions across the United States.

This is a fantastic opportunity to join an established and well-respected organization offering tremendous career growth potential.

Job Title: Edge AI Engineer

Location: 100% Remote (U.S.)

Position Type: Full-time, Direct W2

Salary Range: $100,000–$155,000 Annually

Experience Required: 8+ years

Sponsorship: U.S. Citizens, Green Card Holders, EAD Holders, and H-1B transfer candidates are encouraged to apply. We are unable to sponsor new H-1B visa petitions for this position.

Job Summary:

We are looking for an Edge AI Engineer to design, optimize, and deploy machine learning models that run efficiently on resource-constrained edge devices, including mobile platforms, embedded systems, and specialized accelerators. The role requires deep expertise in model compression, quantization, and hardware-aware optimization, along with strong systems engineering skills to ship reliable AI capabilities outside the data center. The ideal candidate has shipped edge AI in production environments where compute, memory, energy, and connectivity constraints fundamentally shape the engineering trade-offs.

Key Responsibilities

• Design and implement edge AI solutions optimized for diverse hardware including mobile SoCs, NPUs, and embedded accelerators
• Apply quantization, pruning, distillation, and architectural optimization to fit models within edge constraints
• Tune model performance for latency, energy efficiency, and memory footprint on target hardware
• Build cross-platform inference runtimes leveraging frameworks such as TensorFlow Lite, ONNX Runtime, and Core ML
• Optimize models for specific accelerator backends including DSPs, NPUs, and mobile GPUs
• Implement on-device model update, versioning, and rollback workflows that allow safe staged rollouts to large device populations and rapid recovery if a model release behaves unexpectedly in the field
• Design hybrid edge-cloud architectures that gracefully degrade based on connectivity and device capability
• Build telemetry pipelines that respect privacy while enabling continuous improvement
• Collaborate with hardware, firmware, and product teams to align AI capabilities with device constraints
• Implement secure execution paths, model protection, and integrity verification on edge devices
• Develop benchmarking suites that characterize accuracy, latency, and energy trade-offs across devices
• Drive responsible AI considerations including on-device privacy and bias evaluation
• Maintain comprehensive, current technical documentation — including architecture diagrams, design decisions, configuration references, runbooks, and operational procedures — so that the system remains supportable, auditable, and easy to onboard new engineers onto over time
• Stay current with edge AI hardware and software developments, regularly review release notes and community discussions, and translate noteworthy advances into concrete recommendations and adoption proposals for the team

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field
• Eight or more years of experience in ML engineering, with significant work on edge or mobile AI
• Strong proficiency in Python and C++
• Hands-on experience with model compression, quantization, and pruning techniques
• Experience with at least one major edge inference framework
• Solid understanding of mobile and embedded hardware architectures
• Experience deploying ML models to production on mobile or embedded platforms
• Strong performance engineering and profiling skills
• Familiarity with on-device privacy and security considerations
• Strong communication and cross-functional collaboration skills

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with custom NPU or DSP toolchains
• Familiarity with federated lear

FieldAI is where embodied AI meets real robots, real sensors, and real field deployments. We build risk-aware, reliable, field-ready AI systems that tackle challenging robotics problems and unlock the potential of embodied intelligence. Our approach combines frontier research with rigorous engineering, connecting advances in robot learning with the demands of physical systems operating in unpredictable environments.
About the Internship
We are offering spring, summer, and fall 2027 research internships in the Irvine office for master’s and PhD students advancing robotic manipulation.
You will investigate how robots can perform useful physical tasks reliably across diverse objects, environments, and robot platforms. Working closely with researchers and engineers, you will own a focused research project and help translate promising ideas into capabilities that can be tested on hardware and improved through real deployment experience.
Research directions and methods will be shaped by your expertise and the problems we encounter in the field. The goal is to produce original research with measurable impact on what our robots can accomplish.

Real deployment problems: Work on manipulation challenges grounded in customer use cases and operational needs, with opportunities to evaluate beyond controlled laboratory settings.

Develop manipulation capabilities that address meaningful physical tasks in real environments.
Investigate how skills transfer across objects, tasks, environments, and robot platforms.
Address practical challenges such as uncertainty, contact, changing conditions, and failure recovery.
Design experiments that measure task success, generalization, and reliability under realistic operating conditions.
Integrate and validate research on physical robots, collaborating with engineering teams to address system constraints.
Document findings, present results, and contribute to publications or reusable research tools.
What You Have
Current master’s or PhD enrollment in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, AI/ML, or a closely related field.
Research experience in robotic manipulation, robot learning, embodied AI, or a related area.
A strong research or open-source track record, demonstrated through substantive publications, research software, or technically rigorous projects.
Clear ownership of original research or technical development, including implementation and evaluation.
Strong foundations in robotics, machine learning, and experimental design.
Proficiency in Python and/or C++.
Ability to work independently, communicate findings clearly, and collaborate across research and engineering disciplines.
The Extras That Set You Apart
First-author publications at venues such as RSS, CoRL, ICRA, IROS, NeurIPS, ICLR, or ICML, or journals such as RA-L, T-RO, or IJRR.
Significant contributions to open-source robotics or machine learning projects with demonstrated adoption.
Hands-on experience taking research from an initial idea to reliable operation on physical robots.
Experience evaluating robotic systems outside controlled laboratory conditions.
Public research code, datasets, or robot demonstrations showing technical depth and measurable results.

jobs.description:

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are looking for a Manager of Engineering to own the design, build-out, commissioning, and continuous improvement of automation, controls, and electrical systems at SpaceXSI's power generation facility in Southaven. This plant is critical infrastructure for SpaceXSI's AI supercomputers: it must deliver high-reliability power and supporting utilities at scale, with the uptime and response expected of a mission-critical compute campus. 

If it has a gas or steam turbine control system, a switchgear lineup, a plant electrical distribution network, a SCADA/DCS point, a control loop, or a supporting utility/process system (water, wastewater, fuel gas, HVAC, cooling) that must run reliably, this team designs it, specifies it, commissions it, and keeps it running. As a Manager, you will lead a team of engineers in a high-reliability, fast-paced environment. This is a hands-on technical leadership role — you will review P&IDs, challenge control philosophies, dive into DCS/PLC architecture, electrical protection schemes, and commissioning details, not just manage a roadmap. You will scale both the team and the systems as generation capacity and AI compute load grow. 

RESPONSIBILITIES: 

  • Own automation, controls, and electrical scope for power generation assets (gas turbine simple cycle, combined cycle, and steam turbine systems) and plant electrical systems, including DCS/SCADA architecture, PLC systems, turbine control interfaces, switchgear, protection and metering, plant distribution, instrumentation, and control networks — from control philosophy through commissioning and reliability, in compliance with NFPA 70/70B/70E, NESC, and IEEE standards. 
  • Lead controls scope for mechanical and electrical balance-of-plant and supporting utilities, including fuel gas, HVAC, fire protection, compressed air, cooling water, raw water intake, demineralization, wastewater treatment, and industrial gas systems that keep the plant and downstream compute campus online.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Sandbox service team at SpaceXSI builds and maintains a secure, scalable system that gives our models safe, controlled access to computational environments. This infrastructure powers critical workloads across training and product, enabling models to run code, build software, interact with tools, and even control applications with user interfaces. We provision containers and virtual machines on large-scale clusters, granting models interactive control over these remote environments. Our work spans the full stack: from orchestrating massive jobs and resource scheduling at the cluster level, to fine-tuning filesystem performance on nodes. The Sandbox service enables Grok to safely run and test code in real-time for user queries, and supports reinforcement learning in training, where models interactively explore tools ranging from compilers to productivity apps.

You will have the opportunity to work on all modalities of interconnects connecting GPUs and switches both inside and between data centers, including our primary front and backend networks that train Grok and that customers use for inference. Engineers will own all aspects from design and development to build and operations. You will be expected to define and improve team processes and to contribute to scaling and maintenance efforts.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Design, validate, and productize high-speed copper and optical connectivity solutions for AI clusters (100k+ GPU scale).
  • Own vendor due diligence and onboarding for new 1.6T products including AEC and pluggable optical transceivers (DR4/8, FR4) including rigorous bring-up & characterization.
  • Investigate the opportunity for LPO and LRO in our network.
  • Evaluate early co-packaged and near-packaged engines for switches and GPUs.
  • Pathfinding for new interconnect modalities including VCSEL, microLED, THz radio-based solutions to improve network economics and reliability.
  • Work closely with vendors (transceiver, cable, SerDes, DSP, silicon photonics foundries) to influence roadmaps and ensure timely delivery of next-gen solutions.
  • Collaborate with ML training teams to translate workload communication patterns into concrete interconnect topology and optical reconfigurability requirements.
  • Perform system-level simulation of end-to-end fabric performance.
  • Drive failure analysis, root cause, and corrective actions for interconnect-related issues in production clusters through fleet-level metrics gathering and analysis.
  • Contribute to internal tooling and automation for interconnect health monitoring, telemetry, diagnostics, remediation and automated qualification pipelines.
  • Stay current with industry standards (OIF CMIS, IEEE) and emerging technologies (multi-core/hollow-core fiber, 448G SerDes, TFLN, ring resonators)</

jobs.title: Principal Design Verification Engineer
jobs.description:
SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

About the team

SambaNova's RDU is the processor behind our inference systems, and design verification ensures quality and reliability before production. The team owns verification for block, full-chip, and gate-level benches, performance verification, coverage closure, and the emulation and FPGA prototypes.

About the role

SambaNova is looking for a Principal Design Verification Engineer to own verification for  our next-generation RDU, the reconfigurable dataflow silicon behind our machine learning and AI systems. This is a senior individual-contributor role where you'll own the test plan, testbench architecture, coverage model, and sign-off criteria, while shaping the team-wide infrastructure, reuse patterns, and verification practices.

You'll work alongside principal engineers from the design, architecture, compiler, and runtime teams who have built and evolved this verification environment across several generations of silicon, to verify the chip against production ML workloads.

Responsibilities

Some of your responsibilities will include...

  • Own verification end to end for a major subsystem of the RDU: test plan, testbench architecture, coverage model, and sign-off criteria
  • Build the coverage model for your area, set the closure bar, and drive it to closure ahead of tape-out
  • Develop testbench components, agents, checkers, and stimulus at block, full-chip, system, and gate level
  • Serve as the technical authority for verification of your subsystem: review and arbitrate testbench design decisions, and lead debug on the hardest failures
  • Own regression health and failure triage for your area: drive root cause, not just reproduction
  • Verify functional and performance behavior
  • Advance DV methodology beyond your own area: reusable infrastructure, verification IP integration, and AI-assisted verification workflows the rest of the team adopts
  • Contribute to emulation and FPGA prototyping, and support silicon bring-up and post-silicon debug in the lab

jobs.title: Rack Level Manufacturing Test Engineer
jobs.description:
SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide.
